name: Wyoming

context: WY 589 and WY 603 apply to cropland where wind erosion is a resource concern.
WY 588 crosswind ridges suit loamy and clayey soils, not sandy soils.
cover_rules: WY 340: Use the WY-ECS-24 Annual Seed Mix Worksheet; planted PLS per acre must be between 90% to 110% of what was planned.
WY 340: Do not burn cover crop residue and do not harvest cover crops for seed.
WY 340: Seasonal covers used as wind barriers fall under Code 603 and are not cover crops.
residue: WY 329 No Till: crop interval STIR value shall be no greater than 20; do not burn residue.
WY 345 Reduced Till: crop interval STIR value no greater than 80, no primary inversion tillage such as a moldboard plow.
WY 329/345: Use wind erosion prediction technology to set the residue amount and timing needed.
barriers: WY 589: Trap strips at least 15 feet wide if vegetation or stubble is 1 foot or more in height; at least 25 feet if under 1 foot.
WY 603: Barrier rows no more than 36 inches apart; minimum height 1.5 feet and porosity of 40 to 50%.
WY 588: Space ridges no more than four times the designed ridge height.
windbreak: WY 380: Protected zone is 10H on the leeward side and 2H on the windward side.
WY 380: Orient windbreaks perpendicular to the wind causing the concern; choose species taller than the crop.
roughening: WY 609: Roughening is emergency tillage on soils able to form clods; not a primary erosion control practice.
WY 609: Tillage must give random roughness for a 25% reduction in potential erosion rate.
WY 609: Begin roughening on the windward (up wind) edge of the field.
grazing: WY 528: Growing-season use of range grasses will not remove more than 50 percent by weight of current year's growth of key species.
WY 528: Dormant-season use or short grazing with long rest will not remove more than 60 percent of current growth.
WY 528: Browse key species may be used at 65 percent of current year's growth.
WY 528: Pasture (non-rangeland) grazing is timed by leaf length.
drought: WY 528: Keep conservative stocking rates as a drought contingency to limit damage during drought.
WY 528: Develop contingency plans for episodic events such as drought and wildfire.
seeding: WY TN-3: Dormant fall seeding when soil 2 inches deep is 40 degrees for ten consecutive days and before soil freezing.
WY TN-3: Early spring seeding as soon as the soil is workable (not frozen or saturated).
WY 550: Seeding rates are calculated on a pure live seed (PLS) basis; seedings contain a minimum of four native species.
dont_seed: WY 603: Do not recommend buckwheat in rotation with or adjacent (within 30') to commodity wheat.
WY TN-3: Small grains, sudangrass and sorghum can be allelopathic to new seedlings; oats have the least effect.
WY 380: Do not use species on Federal or State invasive species or noxious weed lists.
disturbed: WY 484: Cereal grain straw or grass hay mulch applied for a minimum 70% ground cover.
WY 342: Straw is the preferred mulch; anchor it with rollers or crimpers.
WY 342: Stabilize areas with high rates of soil erosion by wind or water with suited seeding or planting.
dunes: WY 342: Dune plants must survive burial by blowing sand, sand blasting, drought, heat and low nutrient supply.
WY 342: Include sand trapping devices such as sand fences or brush matting where applicable.
WY 342: Follow Wyoming Plant Materials Tech Note 3 for varieties, rates, methods and dates.

seedWin.text: WY TN-3: In precipitation zones 3, 14 and 15 (10-14 inches in zones 3 and 14) seed 10/25 to 5/20 (zone 3: 10/15 to 5/20).
WY TN-3: In the driest zones 4, 5 and 8 (5-9 inches) seed 10/15 to 5/1 or 10/15 to 4/15.
WY TN-3: In zones 1, 2, 10 and 17 (15 to 24+ inches) seed anytime except 6/20 to 9/20.
